what: United Airlines is one of the largest airlines in the world, with the most comprehensive route network of any North American carrier and hubs in Chicago, Denver, Houston, Newark, San Francisco, Los Angeles and Washington.
customers: Leisure and business travellers, corporate accounts, cargo shippers and credit card holders through its loyalty programme.
money: ticket revenue, increasingly weighted to premium cabins
MileagePlus payments from card partners, cargo and maintenance
moat: Hub positions and international route authorities, particularly across the Pacific and Atlantic, that competitors cannot replicate without slots and treaty rights.
risks: Airlines are highly cyclical and fixed costs are large
Newark congestion and air traffic control shortages have caused repeated disruption
opportunities: Analysts see about 42% upside from current levels
Premium cabin and loyalty revenue grow faster and are steadier than economy fares
Limited new aircraft deliveries across the industry restrain capacity growth
watch: Revenue per available seat mile and premium cabin revenue growth.
